title: Practice: how greedy, ε-greedy and UCB choose
note: Three problems since 2026-11-05, greedy and UCB only (ε-greedy left out of the lesson): P3 (greedy against UCB after an unlucky start), P4 (which option UCB picks in one round) and P2 (what one pick does to every score). P1, P5 and P6 need ε-greedy: they are in stash/practice.json. Two rounds of three problems, from the team's item design (P1 to P6). Round 2 repeats round 1's facts in new settings (P4 repeats P2's, P5 P1's and adds UCB, P6 P3's over many rounds), so a correction in round 1 can carry over. Options state only the prediction. Answers and worked solutions stay on the server and are shown on the results page after the final test. Each solution step lists the facts it relies on. `needs` lists the teachable facts without which the answer can't be reached, in the order the steps use them: in the recursive condition Kai can only be right when its notebook holds all of them, correctly explained. Given facts (the setup, averages, trying each option once) are never needed: Kai knows them and the stems repeat them. `beliefs` give, for each needed fact, the answer Kai's assumption for that fact leads to (the fact's `assume` in the graph, word for word; `when: vague` for how Kai reads a vague explanation, where that differs). When needed facts are missing, Kai reasons from the assumption of the first one in `needs` order whose assumption leads somewhere wrong, says that it is guessing, and its wrong answer follows from its own steps. Every wrong option is the prediction of a named misconception (Kai's or a known learner one), so no option can be ruled out without the facts.

items.title: Two cakes
items.prompt: Two cafés test the same two new cakes and score each day's sales out of 10. Cake A is truly better: its days usually score between 7 and 9. Cake B's days always score between 5 and 7. On the first two days both cafés try each cake once; in both, A has an unusually bad day (3) and B scores 6. From then on café 1 uses greedy and café 2 uses UCB. Which café ends up selling mostly cake A?

steps.text: After the first two days, A's average is 3 and B's is 6.
Greedy picks B. B's days score 5 to 7, so B's average stays above 3, greedy never picks A again, and A's average stays at 3.
UCB adds a bonus. Each day B is picked, B's bonus shrinks.
Each day A is not picked, A's bonus grows.
So A's score eventually passes B's, UCB tries A again, A's average rises towards 8, and UCB then mostly sells A.

beliefs.belief: If greedy keeps going, the averages correct themselves over time, so greedy finds the best option in the end.
Every bonus shrinks as rounds pass, whether its option is picked or not.
An option's bonus stays the same while it is not picked.
The bonus of an option that is not picked grows at a steady rate, so a neglected option comes back at regular intervals.
UCB picks the option it is least sure about, the one tried the fewest times, whatever its average.

items.title: Audio tours
items.prompt: A museum app suggests one of four audio tours with UCB. All of the following is for the same round. Tour A averages 6.0 (suggested 50 times), B 6.4 (10 times), C 5.0 (10 times) and D 6.4 (40 times). Which tour does UCB suggest next?
options: It cannot be told without the bonus values

steps.text: UCB suggests the tour with the highest average plus bonus.
A tour's bonus shrinks with every suggestion, so in the same round fewer suggestions means a larger bonus.
B against D: same average, B suggested less, so B scores higher. B against C: same suggestions and so the same bonus, and B has the higher average. B against A: higher average and fewer suggestions.
So B has the highest score, without computing any bonus.

beliefs.belief: UCB picks the option it is least sure about, the one tried the fewest times, whatever its average.
Every bonus shrinks as rounds pass, whether its option is picked or not.

items.title: Exercise types
items.prompt: A language app picks the next exercise type with UCB. Before this round: Flashcards average 6.3, bonus 1.0 (tried 20 times); Dialogues average 5.0, bonus 2.5 (tried 3 times); Listening average 4.0, bonus 1.5 (tried 8 times). UCB picks Dialogues, and the learner scores exactly 5.0 on it. What happens to the three scores (average plus bonus) for the next round?
options: Dialogues' score falls; the other two rise slightly
Dialogues' score falls; the other two stay the same
All three scores stay the same

steps.text: The scores were Flashcards 7.3, Dialogues 7.5 and Listening 5.5, so UCB picked Dialogues.
The new result equals Dialogues' average, so the average stays 5.0.
Dialogues was tried once more, so its bonus shrinks and its score falls.
Flashcards and Listening were not picked, so their bonuses grow slightly with the round number.
